text: Markets are now pricing in rate hikes to ~4.1% by year-end with CPI stuck at 3.4% and surprisingly strong payrolls — this rising-rate environment puts extra pressure on unprofitable and high-multiple holdings in your portfolio, so tighten stops and favor cash-flow-positive names.
Sell RGTI now — you're down nearly 47%, revenue is shrinking at -34%, the company isn't profitable, and every technical and fundamental signal is flashing red, meaning the thesis is broken.

Sell QBTS — a 42% loss combined with negative free cash flow, insiders selling, and over 21% short interest (meaning one in five available shares are being bet against) tells you smart money doesn't believe in this recovery.

Trim IONQ to reduce your exposure — down 25% with no profits, 55% off its highs, and high short interest at 10%, this speculative quantum computing name carries too much risk in a rising-rate environment.
Raise your BMNR stop from $18.11 to $19.03 to lock in more protection, since three consecutive earnings misses and a 64% drawdown from highs mean you want a tighter safety net on this volatile name.

Consider adding to MU — a PE of just 5.9 with nearly 49% revenue growth and a beat streak means this cyclical semiconductor stock looks genuinely undervalued, especially if you can handle short-term volatility.
Consider adding to ADBE — at a PE of just 9.1 with a strong 10% free cash flow yield and insider buying, this profitable software giant looks meaningfully cheap compared to its quality.
Consider adding to GOOGL — a 23 PE with 15% revenue growth, strong free cash flow, and insider confidence makes this one of the safest quality growth names you can own right now.
